answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent economy can enforce dynamic proof-of-burn admission fees. Nodes must verifiably destroy native tokens to register, rendering frictionless replication a fable. Adversaries incur the scarce, non-refundable cost of burned capital per instance to deter them from skimming fee nectar. While dynamic burning cushions registration surges like velvet, wealthy attackers can still absorb the expense, unfairly pricing out honest, low-resource agents.
